Ray Middleton finished first in 54.19 from Nihill (Surrey) and our own Ray Hall and George Williams. The Bels won the team competition from Surrey and M.P.A.A.
Internationals Nihill and Fogg were others to come under the judges ban. Steve Laker-Jones walked well, and it was good to see Bob Barnes making a come-back after 2 years of studies.

His ability to do this and his remarkable pace judgement are models to all athletes. After winning back his National 50 Kilos title from Nihill he is now rarin' to go in the Lugano Cup Final in Italy this October.
However, he paid the penalty for his fast start and dropped to 8th on the homeward journey clocking 2:52:32 against winner Nihill's 2:32:13.

He walked a really well judged race to regain the title he lost to Nihill last year. Always in the first three, he made his effort at the 33 Kilos mark and in the space of 5 miles turned a 1½ minute deficit to Nihill into a 15 seconds lead.

In the R.W.A. 20 miles he beat Wallwork and Thompson, only for Norman Read of New Zealand to beat him by just half a minute; in the R.W.A. 50 kilos he cracked Nihill, only for Thompson to come through and win; and to crown it all in Jamaica he beat both his former victors, only for Wallwork to take his turn at winning.
Our representative in the International 35 Kilos against Western Germany, Ray Middleton, showed great form in finishing second to Nihill by one minute.

Colin Gillett and Chris Martin took silver and bronze in the 200 metres, both in 22.9, and Chris also finished third in the 100 metres (11.5). Our only other senior medal winner was Wil Wesch who took second place behind a National record-breaking Nihill in the 3,000 metres walk.
